title: Puck cylinder side faces mis-indexed; k=n-1 face references a vertex past the puck's block (out-of-range for the last puck)
evidence:
+PUCK_SEG = 16  # smooth circles (the user's 'google-looking circle' markers)
+        puck_verts.append((x, y, z1))
+        for k in range(n):
+            a = 2 * math.pi * k / n
+            puck_verts.append((x + r * math.cos(a), y + r * math.sin(a), z0))
+            puck_verts.append((x + r * math.cos(a), y + r * math.sin(a), z1))
+        for k in range(n):
+            puck_faces.append((base, base + 2 + 2 * k, base + 2 + 2 * ((k + 1) % n)))
+            puck_faces.append((base + 2 + 2 * k, base + 3 + 2 * k, base + 3 + 2 * ((k + 1) % n)))
+            puck_faces.append((base + 2 + 2 * k, base + 2 + 2 * ((k + 1) % n), base + 3 + 2 * ((k + 1) % n)))
detail: PUCK_SEG=16 gives each puck 33 vertices (base..base+32). At k=15 the second face references base+33 — out of range for the last puck (from_pydata error kills the script before any render) and the next puck's center otherwise; side triangles are mis-indexed regardless.
recommended_fix: Index the side quads per ring pair: face2 = (base+2+2k, base+1+2k, base+1+2((k+1)%n)); face3 = (base+2+2k, base+1+2((k+1)%n), base+2+2((k+1)%n)).

title: DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST=3.0 but the street lookup scans only a 3x3-cell (1-tile) neighborhood — nodes 1-3 tiles from a street are never found
detail: Cells are 1x1 tiles, so the ±1-cell scan guarantees only ~1 tile of coverage. Streets 1-3 tiles away are invisible to dublin_node_street: found=false, axis-aligned fallback, and the log message 'no street within 3 tiles' is factually wrong.
recommended_fix: Scan ±ceil(DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST) cells around the node's cell, or lower DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST to ~1.0 so the constant matches the 3x3 neighborhood.

title: 'one-shot log line' claim is false: fmt.printfln fires every frame for every street-less node
evidence:
+// an axis-aligned block + a one-shot log line (amendment #2: flag, never
+		fmt.printfln("[dublin] node at (%.1f, %.1f) has no street within %.0f tiles - axis-aligned block", tx, ty, DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST)
+		top_y := dublin_node_block_draw(v, c, fam, reveal_scale)
detail: draw_building (view.odin:1122) calls dublin_node_block_draw per node per frame; the !found branch logs unconditionally with no one-shot guard. Every far node spams stdout each frame, including during blessed harness captures — contradicting the documented 'one-shot' behavior.
recommended_fix: Gate the log with a per-board set of already-flagged node tiles (or log once during cache build), not inside the per-frame draw path.

title: dublin_node_street claims 'Pure f32 math (the §10.4 rule — no libm)' while calling math.sqrt via the new core:math import
evidence:

detail: The proc comment asserts no libm, but the body calls math.sqrt from the newly added core:math import — the doc contradicts the code it documents and the determinism framing is untrustworthy.

title: ~30 lines of layout_clusters' pool/seed math copy-pasted into main() for blobs/last-mile — guaranteed drift risk
evidence:
+    # rebuild the cluster mapping (same math as layout_clusters' seeds)
+    cands = asset["spawn_candidates"]
+    pool = []
+    for i in range(0, len(cands), 6):
+def layout_clusters(asset, stride=6):
detail: main() re-copies the stride-6 pool build and 4x3 seed selection; the stride is hardcoded twice. Any layout_clusters change silently desyncs blobs/last-mile from terminals/routers — the comment admits the duplication.
recommended_fix: Return seeds (and stride) from layout_clusters and pass them into the last-mile/blob section instead of re-deriving.

title: .scratch/blender_board.png written twice: the docstring's top-down render is clobbered by the zoom-out LOD
evidence:
+Render: .scratch/blender_board.png (2080x1560, board 40x30 units).

detail: The documented main render (OUT_PNG) is silently overwritten by the later zoom-out LOD at the identical path, so the file no longer matches the docstring's described content.

title: int(tree.query_nearest(pt)[0]) crashes the bake on equidistant ties (query_nearest returns all matches by default)
detail: shapely's STRtree.query_nearest returns every tied nearest match by default; int() over a multi-element index array raises TypeError, aborting the bake when a candidate is equidistant to two segments.
